title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_d98
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux/Remaiten botnet infection on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external server? Verify this service exists in the systemd services list by running `systemctl list-units --type=service`.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon.service`. Verify this service exists in the systemd services list.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to network communication or external connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.service` to check the status of the service.

levels.title: Identify Flood Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating the flood of network traffic? Verify this service exists in the systemd services list by running `systemctl list-units --type=service`.
levels.solution: To identify the flood service, examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. The flood service is likely named `bot-flood.service`. Verify this service exists in the systemd services list.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be generating high volumes of network traffic.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bot-flood.service` to check the status of the service.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service? Verify this timer exists in the systemd timers list by running `systemctl list-timers`.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, investigate the systemd timers and look for any timers that might be related to the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism is likely named `system-update-checker.timer`. Verify this timer exists in the systemd timers list.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd timers and look for any timers that might be related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status system-update-checker.timer` to check the status of the timer.
